title: Tor-independent scalar extension of a K-flat augmentation
statement: Let R, A, B be commutative rings and A, B be R-algebras. Suppose Tor_i^R(A,B)=0 for all i>0 [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Let F be an R-K-flat cochain complex [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] and f:F -> B[0] a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], where B is restricted to R. Then termwise extension of scalars A tensor_R f is a quasi-isomorphism of A-complexes [def-weil-module-base-change]. No boundedness assumption on F is imposed.

source.place: Section 06Y5 and Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change; Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change, final affine Tor calculation. Official Stacks pages read online because this clone omits the source files.

proof.text: Take the upstream functorial K-flat resolution p:P -> A[0]. Apply the existing single-support Tor-acyclic tensor lemma in degree zero, transporting hTor along the single-complex degree-zero isomorphism. It proves the termwise tensor of p with B is a quasi-isomorphism. The natural single-factor total tensor isomorphism identifies this with p tensor B[0]. The identity R-linear equivalence on B identifies its algebra R-module structure with restriction of its B-module structure, and whisker exchange gives the natural tensor-square compatibility of that identification.

In the tensor square for p and f, K-flatness of F makes p tensor F a quasi-isomorphism, and K-flatness of P makes P tensor f a quasi-isomorphism. Whisker exchange gives commutativity. The composite through P tensor B[0] is a quasi-isomorphism by the first step. Two-out-of-three therefore gives A[0] tensor f. Transport through the natural single-factor isomorphism to termwise tensor with A. The natural composition comparison identifies this with restriction of scalar extension of f, and restriction detects quasi-isomorphisms. The identity linear equivalence between restriction of A and its algebra R-module structure gives the coefficient comparison. Extension of scalars is additive by its adjunction to restriction, so the functor-composition comparison applies.

theorem scalarAugmentation_quasiIso_of_torIndependent
    {R A B : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    (hTor : ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i →
      IsZero (((CategoryTheory.Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj (ModuleCat.of R A)).obj
        (ModuleCat.of R B)))
    (F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ)
    (hF : (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} R) (.up ℤ)).kFlat F)
    (f : F ⟶ (CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) (0 : ℤ)).obj
      ((restrictScalars (algebraMap R B)).obj (of B B)))
    (hf : QuasiIso f) :
    QuasiIso (((extendScalars (algebraMap R A)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map f)
